notes: Xbox One S Model 1681 as torn down by iFixit, a unit with a Blu-ray drive and a 2 TB hard drive; iFixit says 500 GB and 1 TB versions were coming, so check the drive you have. The power supply is inside the console and its part number is iFixit's replacement listing; the haptic motors are in the controller.

gaps: The power supply part number comes from iFixit's replacement listing (title 'Internal Replacement Part', compatible with the Xbox One S). The teardown names no PSU part number. A retailer listing giving 220 W conflicts with 12 V 10 A and is not used.
The listing's compatible part PA-1131-13MX is kept as the listing states it; no other source checked it.
iFixit's guide 127653 calls the All Digital Edition Model 1681 too, so the disc drive entries apply to the unit torn down (step 10).
Left out: the hard drive (step 9: Seagate Spinpoint M9T ST2000LM003, 2 TB 5400 RPM SATA III), because there is no hard drive part type.
The laser is not named in the guide. The laser entry rests only on the laser caution label (class 2 when open, class 1 laser product) on the DG-6M5S drive in the step 10 photo.
Chips iFixit marks 'likely', 'probably' or 'possibly' (NCP4205, ISD8104, MT7612UN) keep those hedges in the spec.
The controller's haptic motor type and model are not given; the controller's battery model is not given either.
The TI SN75DP159 retimer (step 14) is not listed: no fitting part type.

Datasheets: Diodes AP2127 datasheet opens; Richtek's RT9011 page has no working datasheet link; LCSC's NCP4205 datasheet link returns an HTML page. None found for the Samsung gDDR3, Toshiba eMMC, MediaTek, Nuvoton, MP8757GL or MP2161GJ.
FCC ID C3K1681 was not checked: fccid.io and fcc.report returned HTTP 403 to the researcher.
No source read gives years, so the years field is left out.
method: iFixit Xbox One S Teardown (guide 65572): PDF export (21 pages) read with tools/research.js pdf, plus the API text and step 10 photos; step 2 gives Model 1681.

iFixit Xbox One S Power Supply listing (IF373-009-1, titled Internal Replacement Part): N15-120P1A, compatible part PA-1131-13MX, input 100-240VAC 1.8A 50-60Hz, output 12VDC 10A, compatible with the Xbox One S.
iFixit guide 127653 (Xbox One S All Digital Edition Power Supply Replacement), read through the API: introduction names Model 1681; its parts list is the 'Xbox One S Power Supply'.
Diodes AP2127 datasheet (ordering table lists AP2127K-ADJTRG1) opened as a PDF; LCSC listing C904499 (onsemi NCP4205MNTXG) and Richtek's RT9011 page open and name the chips.
Refused to the researcher: fccid.io and fcc.report (HTTP 403).

comps.spec: X949211-001 SoC: 1.75 GHz AMD 'Jaguar' 8-core CPU with a 914 MHz AMD Radeon GPU (step 14)
Samsung K4W4G1646E-BC1A 4 Gb (512 MB) 'gDDR3' SDRAM as iFixit labels it, 16 chips for 8 GB in total (step 14)
Toshiba THGBMFG6C1LBAIL 8 GB eMMC NAND flash (step 14)
ON Semiconductor NCP4205, which iFixit calls likely an iteration of the NCP4204 and probably a CPU power-phase PWM controller (step 14)
Monolithic Power Systems MP8757GL, 7 A / 18 V synchronous step-down converter (step 16)
Monolithic Power Systems MP2161GJ, 2 A / 6 V synchronous step-down converter (step 16)
Linear regulators (step 16): Richtek RT9011-JGPQV 300 mA dual LDO; Diodes AP2127K-ADJTRG1 300 mA LDO; ON Semiconductor CAT6243DCADJ 1 A LDO
MediaTek MT7612UN, which iFixit says is likely a variation of the MT7612U 2x2 802.11ac Wi-Fi module (step 8)
Single 120 mm fan in the thermal system (step 13)
Aluminium heat sink with a copper heat pipe set, held to the board by an X-shaped bracket (steps 12 and 13)
Internal power supply module (iFixit's replacement listing for the Xbox One S), part N15-120P1A, compatible part PA-1131-13MX: input 100-240 VAC 1.8 A 50-60 Hz; output 12 VDC 10 A
Laser in the Philips/Lite-On DG-6M5S BD-ROM drive (step 10): the drive label carries a laser caution, class 2 laser radiation when open, and reads class 1 laser product
Four haptic feedback motors in the controller (step 18)
Nuvoton ISD8104 2 W class AB audio amplifier, marked likely by iFixit (step 15)
